assumptions: Assay sensitivity is adequate to detect capture-positive signal and protected bioactivity at post-processing concentrations.
Capture reagents and particle counters are available and their compatibility with excipients can be controlled for.
Candidate in vitro bioassay (LPS-stimulated human iPSC-microglia cytokine readout) is a relevant, reproducible proxy for program-relevant anti-inflammatory activity.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 emphasizes orthogonal intact-EV analytics and warns that handling, buffers, and process exposures can alter membrane integrity or marker accessibility; large-animal intranasal biodistribution failures further heighten the need to test whether formulation or device exposures destroy EV-associated signatures even when particle counts remain similar (evidence: ev-misev2023-quality-framework, ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution, ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative preservation (yes/no) of capture co-localization and detergent/protease-sensitive capture signal after exposure.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV identity and purity
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Compatibility-preservation of the orthogonal intact-EV signature will be used to accept or reject formulation/device candidates for further development; numeric limits are not yet asserted.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative detection (presence/absence) of capture-positive, particle-co-localized signal in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue samples.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Intranasal biodistribution (short-interval detectability)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: In vivo short-interval recovery in nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after dosing with a formulation/device condition that passed in vitro compatibility supports downstream delivery decisions (no numeric thresholds asserted).

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative preservation (yes/no) of protected anti-inflammatory readout (e.g., LPS-induced cytokine reduction) in capture-positive fractions and loss after detergent/protease treatment.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Membrane-protected neuroinflammation-modulating bioactivity
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: A membrane-protected, detergent/protease-sensitive in vitro bioactivity that is preserved after formulation/device exposures will be used as a functional compatibility metric without asserting mechanism or potency numeric limits.

edges.competing_explanation: Apparent loss of capture signal could reflect assay interference by excipient components rather than true membrane damage.
edges.missing_experiment: Matrixed capture-reagent compatibility controls and detergent/protease protection checks for each excipient and device-exposure condition.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal analytics and notes processing sensitivity but does not quantify specific excipient or device thresholds.

edges.competing_explanation: In vitro bioactivity could be mediated by soluble factors that survive or are unaffected by excipients, so bioactivity preservation might not track with membrane-protection.
edges.missing_experiment: Parallel identity and protected-bioactivity readouts after formulation/device exposures.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: rodent functional observations exist but do not establish that preserved membrane protection or identity metrics are required for activity; linkage must be tested.

edges.competing_explanation: Delivery failures in large animals may reflect administration route or species-specific clearance independent of formulation/device compatibility.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo detection after model-selected formulation/device exposures to confirm that in vitro compatibility predicts in vivo recoverability.
edges.uncertainty: High: large-animal nasal delivery uncertainty increases priority of compatibility testing, but does not identify which excipients or device parameters are causal for detectability loss.

nodes.statement: Contact with specific nasal formulation excipient classes (ionic strength extremes, non-ionic surfactants, chelators) or passage through delivery-device geometries that create shear can alter EV membrane integrity or surface-marker accessibility without changing bulk particle counts.

Loss of membrane integrity or mask­ing of surface epitopes will abolish an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) while particle counters report limited change.

If a candidate formulation/device condition preserves the orthogonal intact-EV signature, the same condition will also preserve a membrane-protected in vitro neuroinflammation-modulating bioactivity (or conversely, loss of the signature will correlate with loss of membrane-protected bioactivity).

Defining formulation/device compatibility by preservation of both the orthogonal identity signature and membrane-protected bioactivity enables a non-assumptive, functional compatibility gate suitable for CMC and comparability decisions.

competing_explanations: Bioactivity loss after exposure may reflect selective removal of an active soluble factor rather than EV membrane disruption.
Apparent loss of capture signal could be due to direct chemical interference of excipient with the capture reagent rather than loss of EV integrity.
dependencies: Access to a short list of candidate nasal excipient classes prioritized by CMC and regulatory input
Device shear-profile characterization (vendor or bench simulation)
design_question: Daily question: Which specific nasal vehicle excipient classes and device shear exposures preserve an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) and a matched in vitro membrane-protected anti-inflammatory bioactivity, versus those that abolish both signatures despite similar bulk particle counts?
expected_measurable_effect: Qualitative partitioning of formulation/device conditions into 'compatibility-pass' (preserve capture-positive/particle-peak co-localization and detergent/protease-sensitive protected bioactivity) versus 'compatibility-fail' (loss of capture co-localization and loss/insensitivity of bioactivity) across independent lots and capture-reagent compatibility controls.

experiment.assay: Parallel orthogonal workflows: (1) density/size fractionation with particle counting per fraction and immuno-capture ELISA/bead-capture on intact fractions to assess co-localization; (2) protease/RNase protection ± detergent on captured material to test membrane protection; (3) apply matched fraction eluates to the in vitro neuroinflammation assay (LPS-challenged microglia readout) to test protected bioactivity; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratios per fraction; (5) capture-reagent buffer-compatibility panels to detect assay interference.
experiment.comparator: Matrixed, paired comparisons per conditioned-medium lot: (A) no-exposure control (aliquot in baseline buffer, no device pass), versus (B...N) each formulation buffer condition ± device-shear exposure (low/mid/high). Include detergent/protease-disrupted aliquots as negative membrane-protection controls and capture-reagent compatibility controls (capture reagent incubated with formulation buffer alone).
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EV prep processed identically; assay positive control: dexamethasone in bioassay. Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer-only fractions. Capture-compatibility controls for each excipient condition.
dependencies: Availability of ≥3 independent conditioned-medium production lots from the same source-cell bank for reproducibility testing
Access to capture reagents, particle counters, and fractionation equipment with sufficient sensitivity
Laboratory capability for the selected in vitro neuroinflammation assay
Device-shear characterization data or rigs to simulate device exposures
Human approvals for material handling and biosafety
experiment.failure_criterion: After capture-compatibility controls, no tested formulation/device condition reproducibly preserves both the orthogonal intact-EV signature and membrane-protected bioactivity across ≥3 lots (i.e., all conditions either abolish signature or produce assay-interference indistinguishable from true loss).
experiment.falsification_outcome: If the failure criterion is met, the hypothesis is falsified for the tested excipient/device envelope: the program should not assume formulation/device compatibility preserves intact-EV identity or protected bioactivity, and must investigate alternative approaches (immediate capture/lyophilization, secretome-centric product definition, or alternative delivery routes).
experiment.hypothesis_tested: Specific formulation excipient classes and delivery-device shear exposures will either preserve or abolish an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks + detergent/protease sensitivity) and a matched membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory bioactivity; conditions that preserve both are compatible for intranasal use without assuming prior EV identity.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative preservation (yes/no) per condition of (A) particle-count peak co-localizing with capture-positive fraction and detergent/protease-sensitive loss of capture signal, and (B) presence of membrane-protected anti-inflammatory effect in capture-positive fraction eluates that is abolished after detergent/protease treatment.
experiment.question: Which nasal excipient classes and device-shear exposures preserve the orthogonal intact-EV signature and membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory bioactivity versus those that abolish both, independent of bulk particle counts?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed to yield an enriched small-EV fraction (program-defined bounded fraction) in sufficient volume for matrixing

A panel of candidate formulation buffers/excipient classes (matrix across pH, ionic strength, osmolarity, non-ionic surfactant at low and moderate concentrations, chelator presence/absence, sugar/polyol stabilizers) representative of nasal-spray formulations
Device-shear simulation rigs or representative nasal spray devices with characterized shear/pressure profiles (low-, mid-, high-shear exposures) to pass aliquots through device geometries
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV surface markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5 capture reagents) and capture-compatibility control reagents
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Detergent (e.g., Triton X-100) for membrane disruption controls
Density-fractionation materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Standardized in vitro neuroinflammation assay platform (e.g., LPS-stimulated human iPSC-derived microglia or primary microglia with IL-6/TNF-α readout via ELISA or multiplex)
Total protein assay reagents, buffers, and consumables
Buffer-only and positive control small EV preparation (commercial or lab-validated) and a known anti-inflammatory assay control (e.g., dexamethasone)
secondary_readouts: Capture-signal-to-noise and buffer-compatibility metrics to exclude assay interference
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n ≥ 3 independent conditioned-medium lots)
Mass and particle recovery (yield) after formulation/device exposure
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: For ≥1 formulation excipient class (and corresponding device-shear envelope), across ≥3 independent conditioned-medium lots, the condition reproducibly preserves both (A) the orthogonal intact-EV identity signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive capture signal) and (B) a membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory bioactivity in capture-positive fractions, while capture-compatibility controls confirm signal is not assay interference.

explicit_inferences: Inference: Preservation of an orthogonal intact-EV identity signature is necessary (but not proven sufficient) for preserving a membrane-protected bioactivity after formulation/device exposure; this must be empirically tested with matched controls.
Inference: Capture-reagent compatibility checks are required to distinguish assay interference from true membrane damage.
falsification_criteria: If, after appropriate capture-reagent compatibility controls, no formulation or device condition shows reproducible preservation of both the orthogonal intact-EV signature and membrane-protected bioactivity across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots, the hypothesis is falsified for the tested excipient/device envelope and the program must treat compatibility as unresolved and consider alternative vehicle strategies (e.g., immediate capture, lyophilized formats, or secretome-centric product definition).
human_decisions_required: Select prioritized excipient classes and concentrations for the initial matrix (CMC/formulation lead)
Decide acceptable device-shear envelope to simulate (formulation + device engineering)
Approve selection of the in vitro neuroinflammation assay platform and success readout (preclinical lead)
manufacturability_assessment: Feasible: matrixed compatibility testing across a limited excipient class set and a small set of device-shear simulations is manageable in Stage-1; positive compatibility gates would simplify downstream CMC by constraining excipient and device choices.
manufacturing_rationale: Formulation excipients and device shear are common, controllable contributors to post-production attribute loss; defining a preservative compatibility envelope early protects downstream CMC and comparability work and reduces risk of scale-up failures.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture + particle-count co-localization + detergent/protease protection) and a matched in vitro membrane-protected functional assay run in parallel for each condition; include capture-reagent compatibility and buffer controls; require >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots per tested condition for reproducibility.
novelty_statement: Novel discriminant: This hypothesis defines a compatibility test that jointly requires preservation of an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature AND a matched membrane-protected functional readout after formulation and device-shear exposures. Prior program hypotheses tested fractionation, source senescence, scale effects, or process-induced signature loss but did not propose a single matrixed formulation+device compatibility experiment that treats formulation-induced assay interference explicitly and requires parallel protected-bioactivity verification. This explicitly bridges formulation/device compatibility decisions to orthogonal intact-EV identity and protected functional readouts rather than relying on particle counts or repeat of prior fractionation/process experiments.
principal_risks: Apparent signal loss due to capture-reagent/excipient interference rather than true EV damage (mitigate with matrixed capture-compatibility controls).
Insufficient assay sensitivity for low-biomass post-exposure samples leading to false negatives.
In vitro compatibility may not predict in vivo short-interval recoverability or large-animal translation.
proposed_potency_relationship: Exploratory: preservation of membrane-protected bioactivity in capture-positive fractions will be used as an initial functional compatibility readout; not asserted as a validated potency assay.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, adopt a compatibility gate: allowed formulation excipient classes and device-shear exposure envelope that preserve an orthogonal intact-EV identity signature plus membrane-protected bioactivity (used as a process/formulation compatibility acceptance attribute), distinct from bulk-particle-based compatibility criteria.
title: Hypothesis: Specific intranasal formulation excipients and delivery-device shear preserve or abolish an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature and membrane-protected bioactivity — enabling a compatibility test that does not assume pre-existing EV identity
